builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
summary: The scheme replaces prior secure aggregation protocols that either force all clients onto a common finite group or leak partial aggregates and individual update segments when clients use heterogeneous quantization levels, by secret-sharing updates from distinct algebraic groups via identical linear integer systems with a (T+1, N) threshold black-box construction. It costs additional cryptographic machinery: secret share generation per client, communication overhead for distributing shares, and protocol complexity that must accommodate dropouts and up to T server-colluding semi-honest clients. It can fail in practice if the assumed threat model (semi-honest collusion bounded by T) is exceeded, if dropout rates exceed the reconstruction threshold, or if the deployment does not actually involve cross-device federated learning, in which case the privacy guarantee is irrelevant.
rationale: This is a specialized cryptographic protocol for federated learning privacy, relevant only if the reader deploys FL with untrusted servers, and the abstract provides no quantified efficiency claim to evaluate against a 24 GB GPU budget.
technique: Secure aggregation with heterogeneous client quantization
